In a uniform magnetic field, moving charged particle experiences magnetic force perpendicular to its direction of motion, which is called Lorentz force and is given as
F = q(v × B) i.e. F ⊥ v
where, v = velocity, q = charge and B = magnetic field
i.e. force on charged particle always remains perpendicular to its velocity i.e. its displacement.
Hence, work done= F·s
          = Fscos90° = 0
Hence, according to work-energy theorem,
ΔEK = W = 0
i.e. kinetic energy = constant.
Hence, in uniform magnetic field, speed and energy remains the same for moving charged particle. Therefore, both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
"

The order of basicity of amines in the gaseous phase follows the expected order: tertiary amine > secondary amine > primary amine > NH3. The trend is not regular in the aqueous state the substituted ammonium cations get stabilised not only by electron releasing effect of the alkyl group (+I) but also by solvation with water molecules. The greater the size of the ion, lesser will be the solvation and the less stabilised is the ion. The order of stability of ions are as follows :

Thus, the order of basicity of aliphatic amines should be: primary > secondary > tertiary, which is opposite to the inductive effect-based order. Therefore, the change of nature of the alkyl group, e.g., from –CH3 to –C2H5 results in change of the order of basic strength. Thus, there is a subtle interplay of the inductive effect, solvation effect and steric hinderance of the alkyl group which decides the basic strength of alkyl amines in the aqueous state.
